exchanges.question: Can you explain how much of the 9%-11% September quarter growth deceleration versus June is supply constraints versus FX, and what supply constraints beyond advanced SOCs are broadening?
exchanges.answer: Foreign exchange headwind is around 2.5 percentage points to year-over-year growth rate. Supply constraint impact is expected to increase significantly sequentially from June to September, affecting iPhone, Mac, and iPad. During June, constraints were primarily on Mac, driven by limited flexibility in the supply chain and availability of advanced nodes for SoCs. For September, Tim expects high levels of demand but significantly increased supply constraints with less supply chain flexibility to remedy it.

exchanges.question: Does Apple's greater sourcing flexibility for memory aim to ensure supply and mitigate inflation, or primarily to preserve customer value proposition?
exchanges.answer: Memory costs rose from December to March quarter, expected to rise significantly again in June, and will rise even higher in September. Offsets include carry-in inventory benefits, though benefit will decrease over time, and lower costs on non-memory components. Beyond September, market pricing for memory expected to continue increasing with potential increasing impact on the business. DRAM market has three suppliers; more suppliers could help supply and potentially pricing.

exchanges.question: What are expected adoption rates for Apple Upgrade Program across install base, and will it shorten replacement cycles equally across iPhone, Mac, and iPad?
exchanges.answer: Apple Upgrade makes it easier for customers to get latest products with leasing plan that's right for them, leveraging Apple's higher residual values versus competitors. Available in US retail stores, not widely in all channels. Early customer feedback is quite positive. Kevan noted it's only available in the U.S. right now.

exchanges.question: What learnings from iOS 27 and Apple Intelligence public beta inform compute costs, capital recovery, and iCloud+ strategy?
exchanges.answer: Siri AI has received overwhelmingly positive feedback from WWDC, developer beta, and public beta released weeks ago. AI that is private, personal-context based, and integrated across OS is a very big idea. Early on compute cost strategy; people will have upgrade possibilities on iCloud+ to buy up the stack. Overall extremely excited about product direction.

exchanges.question: Street expects 12% September growth but you guided 10%; if FX accounts for difference, what are December quarter supply constraint impacts?
exchanges.answer: Primary constraint is advanced nodes for SoCs, not a regular supply issue but a demand forecast issue. iPhone grew 22% and Mac grew 29%, better than expected. Supply chain has less flexibility than normal. Kevan stated dynamics combined with FX impact built into 9%-11% September guidance; beyond September no color is provided.

exchanges.question: Could alternative silicon suppliers like those building Arizona fab help alleviate your silicon constraints in reasonable timeframe?
exchanges.answer: This is not a partner or supplier issue. The constraints stem from incredibly strong iPhone and Mac product cycles with demand beyond expectation. Arizona fab supplies over 100 million components this year as part of $600 billion US commitment, ramping well and producing successfully.

exchanges.question: Will you pursue multi-year LTAs with suppliers for supply access at pre-agreed prices, and does pricing strategy protect product gross profit dollars or gross margins?
exchanges.answer: Prices were raised reluctantly due to 100-year flood of memory pricing with exponential increases. Philosophy looks at units, revenue, and margin together to make business judgment; not a mathematical formula or single dimension. Think about it over long term rather than 90-day clock.

exchanges.question: Services grew 12% versus guidance, below 10% implied for September. Explain deceleration drivers and whether App Store headwinds relate to AI reprioritizing user time?
exchanges.answer: Foreign exchange was main driver of growth rate change from March to June. Other factors: no theatrical F1 release this year versus prior year, and App Store headwinds in mobile gaming. App Store changes in certain countries and court ruling on link-out transactions in US impacted performance. Despite this, App Store set June quarter record. Strong double-digit growth in cloud, video, payment, advertising. Set records in every category.

exchanges.question: Has demand pull-forward occurred in consumer or enterprise/education markets, and is this factored into forward views?
exchanges.answer: iPhone has been running 22% growth rate year to date. It's not obvious in the data that pull-forward has occurred. Price increases on iPad and Mac occurred; price elasticity too early to conclude. Channel inventory adjustments take time for consumer response to be understood in weeks ahead.

exchanges.question: Does AI proliferation at edge open additional addressable market opportunities for Apple beyond current products?
exchanges.answer: Enormous opportunities for Apple moving forward in AI. Siri AI feedback is excellent. Ability to run percentage of requests on-device is strategic and competitive advantage. Extremely excited about these opportunities.

exchanges.question: Will Siri AI change Apple's capital intensity given on-device and distributed compute, with some backend requests to first-party and third-party cloud?
exchanges.answer: Uses hybrid model with some third-party cloud and own data centers. Generally OpEx and AI spending growing significantly. Other P&L locations like COGS also have AI expenditures. What Siri AI does on cost side uncertain. Also ability for heavy users to move up iCloud Plans provides recovery option.

exchanges.question: How is competitive landscape changing, particularly with OpenAI or SpaceX potentially building AI-enabled phones that bypass carrier infrastructure?
exchanges.answer: There is so much opportunity for Apple with everything happening in this space. Apple is focused on its plans and very excited about them.

exchanges.question: You mentioned Siri AI won't launch initially in China and Europe. What are updated thoughts on launch timing and hurdles needed in those regions?
exchanges.answer: EU: Working closely with commission; complete desire is to launch everywhere simultaneously. Not been able to do so in EU. Working closely to get to something allowing Siri AI offer there. Will be offered on Mac as not covered by same regulations as iPhone/iPad. China: Last week received approval for original Apple Intelligence features like cleanup. Working through rollout; more work required for Siri AI, at front end of that.

exchanges.question: Walk through sequential gross margin drivers from 48% adjusted in June to 46.5% September guidance, separating FX from commodity costs and memory?
exchanges.answer: More than 100% of 120 bps change from March 49.3% to June 48.1% explained by memory cost changes. Same dynamics for 160 bps change from June 48.1% to September 46.5% midpoint. Partial offsets from carry-in inventory benefits, lower non-memory component costs, favorable mix. FX minimal impact versus memory. Sequential change from March to September really driven by memory.
